mainText.text: Lakes are good examples of biodiversity, often having a variety of species and ecological processes. On a microscopic scale, entire communities of bacteria and single-celled protists interact, influencing nutrient availability for plants and animals. For example, a healthy population of decomposer bacteria breaks down dead organic matter, recycling essential nutrients back into the water for aquatic plants and microscopic algae at the base of the food web.

On a macroscopic scale, top predators like large fish and birds impact the population size of every species in the food web through activities like predation and competition. And when an organism of any size dies in the lake, its remains provide nutrients for decomposer bacteria. Such interactions between microscopic and macroscopic life forms significantly shape the lake ecosystem's overall health and productivity.

mainText.text: Lakes are good examples of biodiversity, often having a variety of species and ecological processes. On a microscopic scale, entire communities of bacteria and single-celled protists interact, influencing nutrient availability for plants and animals. For example, a healthy population of decomposer bacteria breaks down dead organic matter, recycling essential nutrients back into the water for aquatic plants and microscopic algae at the base of the food web.

On a macroscopic scale, top predators like large fish and birds impact the population size of every species in the food web through activities like predation and competition. And when an organism of any size dies in the lake, its remains provide nutrients for decomposer bacteria. Such interactions between microscopic and macroscopic life forms significantly shape the lake ecosystem's overall health and productivity.

mainText.text: Lakes are good examples of biodiversity, often having a variety of species and ecological processes. On a microscopic scale, entire communities of bacteria and single-celled protists interact, influencing nutrient availability for plants and animals. For example, a healthy population of decomposer bacteria breaks down dead organic matter, recycling essential nutrients back into the water for aquatic plants and microscopic algae at the base of the food web.

On a macroscopic scale, top predators like large fish and birds impact the population size of every species in the food web through activities like predation and competition. And when an organism of any size dies in the lake, its remains provide nutrients for decomposer bacteria. Such interactions between microscopic and macroscopic life forms significantly shape the lake ecosystem's overall health and productivity.
